text.label: Text: Why proof sells
text.value: Why proof sells

text.label: Heading: A stranger does not buy what you say. They buy what other pe
text.value: A stranger does not buy what you say. They buy what other people say about you.

text.label: Text: Start with the stranger.
text.value: Start with the stranger.

text.label: Text: Picture somebody who found you last night. They watched a cl
text.value: Picture somebody who found you last night. They watched a clip, liked what you said, and clicked through to your website. They do not know you. They have been burned before by somebody who talked a good game. So before they spend a dollar, they go looking for one thing: has this worked for a person like me? Everything you say about yourself is a sales pitch in their eyes. What your students, clients and readers say is evidence. That is the difference.

text.label: Text: Why you have so little.
text.value: Why you have so little.

text.label: Text: Most coaches, authors and influencers have helped far more p
text.value: Most coaches, authors and influencers have helped far more people than their reviews show. The work was good. The clients were happy. Nobody asked. Or somebody asked once, weeks later, in a group message, and a few people answered. That is not laziness. Asking feels awkward, it is easy to put off, and you are busy doing the actual work. So years of results sit in private messages and thank-you notes where no buyer will ever see them. You did the hard part and never collected the receipt.

text.label: Text: What that costs you.
text.value: What that costs you.

text.label: Text: You taught them. Somebody else got paid. That is what thin p
text.value: You taught them. Somebody else got paid. That is what thin proof costs. A follower can watch you for a year, enjoy every minute, and still buy from the person down the feed who has a wall of happy clients. A clip from you says you know your subject. A review from a student says it worked for somebody. People need to see you and hear from you seven to ten times before they trust you enough to pay, and proof is what makes each of those times count.

text.label: Text: What a talent agent does.
text.value: What a talent agent does.

text.label: Text: A talent agent never walks into a room and says the talent i
text.value: A talent agent never walks into a room and says the talent is great. He hands over what other people said and lets that do the talking. That is the job this system does for you. Self-promotion is part of the work now, whatever you do for a living, and you still have to show up and be seen. But telling strangers how good you are is the one kind you should never have to do yourself. As your modern day talent agency, my team and I make sure your students, clients and readers do that bragging for you.

text.label: Text: So we build the asker.
text.value: So we build the asker.

text.label: Text: This system exists to fix that one gap. It is an AI employee
text.value: This system exists to fix that one gap. It is an AI employee whose whole job is to stay in touch with the people you are already helping, find out how it is going, and ask the happy ones to say so. You get two things out of it. A review is what they write in public, where strangers check you out. A testimonial is their story, in their own words or on video, on your website. It does not get embarrassed. It does not forget. My team and I set it up around the way your program, your book or your coaching runs, and from then on every person gets asked. Not most of them. Every one.

text.label: Text: Why it is system four.
text.value: Why it is system four.

text.label: Text: The order of the six never changes, and here is what happens
text.value: The order of the six never changes, and here is what happens if you try this one early. With no website of your own, a great review has nowhere to live except somebody else's page. With nothing bringing people in, nobody new ever reads it. With nobody answering, the stranger it convinced sends a message and hears nothing back. So it goes in fourth, when there are people to ask and a place to show what they said. From there it keeps paying you for work you already did, because every new client becomes the next review.

props.text: The ask goes out while they are still happy.

Not three days later when somebody remembers. There are two good moments, and your AI employee is watching for both. The first is the first real win, the day a student gets a result they could not get before. The second is the finish. A person is proudest of what they did on those two days, and those are the days they will gladly tell the world about it. A week later they are back in their own life and your request is one more thing in a full inbox. You did not get worse in that week. You just asked late. Your AI employee does not ask late, because it is not waiting on anybody to remember.

text.value: Step by step

text.label: Heading: Exactly how every client, student and reader gets asked.
text.value: Exactly how every client, student and reader gets asked.

text.label: Text: First, we learn your program.
text.value: First, we learn your program.

text.label: Text: Before anything goes out, my team and I sit down with you an
text.value: Before anything goes out, my team and I sit down with you and walk through how a person moves through what you sell. Where does it start? Where do people usually get stuck? Where do they get their first win? Where does it end? Those are the points that matter, and they are different for a twelve week coaching program than for an e-book somebody reads in a weekend. You tell us once. We build the check-ins around those moments, in your words, so they sound like you.

text.label: Text: Then it watches the calendar.
text.value: Then it watches the calendar.

text.label: Text: From the day somebody enrols or buys, your AI employee knows
text.value: From the day somebody enrols or buys, your AI employee knows where they are. It is following the program dates and the payments, so it knows when a student hits the halfway point or a reader has had time to get through the book. Nobody on your team keeps a list. Nobody sets a reminder. When a person reaches one of the moments you named, the check-in goes out on its own, to that one person, at that point in their own journey.

text.label: Text: The check-in is short.
text.value: The check-in is short.

text.label: Text: It is a quick, friendly question about how things are going,
text.value: It is a quick, friendly question about how things are going, sent as a message on their phone. It takes them a few seconds to answer. It is not a long form and it is not a sales pitch. People answer because it is easy and because it feels like you care how they are doing, which you do. You just never had the hours to ask every single one of them. Now every one of them hears from you.

text.label: Text: If somebody is unhappy.
text.value: If somebody is unhappy.

text.label: Text: You find out the same day, privately, while the program is s
text.value: You find out the same day, privately, while the program is still running. The note you get is short. It tells you who it is, where they are in your program and what they said, in their own words. Your AI employee does not try to fix it or talk them out of it. That one is not its to answer. It is yours. A student who is stuck in the middle is a problem you can fix with one phone call. You do not need a script. You ask what happened, you listen, and you put right what you can. The same student, ignored until the end, is a refund request or a bad review.

text.label: Text: If somebody is happy.
text.value: If somebody is happy.

text.label: Text: They get asked right then, while the good feeling is fresh.
text.value: They get asked right then, while the good feeling is fresh. The message carries the link, so there is nothing to look for and no new account to open. Some will write a few lines in public. That is the review. Some will tell the whole story, in writing or on video, for your website. That is the testimonial. Either one is gold. And to be plain about it, we do not hide the unhappy ones. Anybody can say whatever they like about you, anywhere. When a bad one does go public, it sits among a lot of good ones, which is about what a stranger expects to see.

text.label: Text: Readers get asked too.
text.value: Readers get asked too.

text.label: Text: This is not only for a high priced program. The person who b
text.value: This is not only for a high priced program. The person who bought your e-book on your website is a customer, and we know who they are because they bought it from you and not from a platform. They get a check-in once they have had time to read it. A reader who loved the book is asked to say so. That review sits beside the book on your website, and it helps the next visitor decide to buy it.

text.label: Text: What your week looks like.
text.value: What your week looks like.

text.label: Text: You do not send anything. You do not chase anybody. You do n
text.value: You do not send anything. You do not chase anybody. You do not keep a list of who to ask. What you see is a short note when a student needs a call, and new reviews showing up with your name on them. An expert's income is a direct reflection of the time and effort they put into their business. Your part here is the conversations only you can have. Your AI employee does the rest, day and night, with my team behind it and me on your account, and it does it for every person from now on.

text.label: Text: If you have helped far more people than your reviews show, t
text.value: If you have helped far more people than your reviews show, tell us about it.

props.text: And then they belong on your own website.

Now the part nobody thinks about. You earned those reviews. Right now they live on a page that also lists other people who teach what you teach, so the proof you worked years for is doing its selling inside somebody else's shopping list. Think about what that means. Somebody hears you on a podcast, likes you, and looks you up. The first thing they are shown is you and a row of other choices. Your own happy students just walked that person into a comparison. Nobody did anything wrong. That is simply how those pages are built. So we keep the reviews there, and we also bring them home.

This is Google, your social profile, the page where your book is sold. Your rating sits beside everybody else's, with a list of other choices. The buyer is comparing. That is what those pages are built to make them do. You do not own them and you do not decide what sits next to your name. They still matter, because that is where a stranger checks whether you are real. It is just not where you want them to make up their mind.

The same reviews, pulled in and kept current, with nobody else on the screen, next to your story, your program and a button that books the call. Nothing to compare against. When a new review comes in, it shows up here without you lifting a finger. The person reading it is one tap from your e-book, one tap from your podcast and one tap from a call with you. This is the page you own, so this is the page where the proof gets to finish its work.

Both, ideally. The profile is how they find you. Your site is where the reviews finish the job. One gets you looked up and trusted by people who have never heard your name. The other is where the person who already likes you reads what your students said, sees no other choices, and books the call.
